dataset.label: Public dataset facts
dataset.statement: PopSign ASL v1.0 (CC BY 4.0) is a small, isolated five-prompt corpus. A session count is not defined by the public evidence.

baseline.label: Signer-held-out logistic baseline
baseline.statement: These are real held-out results for the five-class logistic baseline, not performance for the browser candidate.

architecture.label: Development architecture evidence
architecture.statement: Three signer-grouped development folds support carrying the hand-local TCN architecture forward. They do not measure the exact browser checkpoint.

calibration.label: Constructed calibration mechanics
calibration.statement: The exact candidate used reused development examples and three constructed transition fragments. Temperature 0.050 hit the search boundary; the selected 0% threshold abstained on no rows. This checks mechanics, not model quality or natural use.

runtime.label: Runtime equivalence evidence
runtime.statement: The exported candidate matched its reference implementation on the measured fixtures. This does not establish recognition quality or behavior on unmeasured inputs.

browser.label: Reference-machine browser measurement
browser.statement: One reference-machine benchmark measured cold and warm Chromium runs on a Windows computer under a generated no-person camera workload.
browser.environment: Chromium 151.0.7922.34; Windows 10.0.26200 x64; Intel i9-14900HX; 32 logical CPUs; WASM with one thread.
browser.sampleNote: Each inference percentile uses 5 warmups followed by 50 measured calls.
limitations: One machine and browser cannot predict other devices.
The generated no-person workload is easier than real hand video.
Inference timing excludes capture, worker transfer, event detection, and rendering.
Memory was unavailable, and these timings are not CI thresholds.

items.label: Exact-candidate locked-test performance
items.statement: The exact browser candidate has not been evaluated on the locked test set.

items.label: Natural other movement
items.statement: The available other examples are constructed transition fragments, not natural recordings.

items.label: Natural continuous false activations
items.statement: Constructed replay checks scorer behavior but cannot estimate false activations in natural sessions.

items.label: Fairness
items.statement: The current evidence does not support subgroup comparisons.

items.label: Robustness
items.statement: The current evidence does not establish behavior across varied capture conditions or devices.

items.label: Population performance
items.statement: This small corpus cannot support broad population or sign-language generalization claims.
